parsed.why: Protective state shield, public-accommodation anti-discrimination, hate-crime recourse and no facility ban materially mitigate hostile national border regime; old custody placement adds small residual risk.

State facility ban, absent anti-discrimination/hate-crime recourse and closed documents add universal exposure below hostile national regime; patchy local protections do not offset enacted restriction.
Strong public-accommodation, facility, hate-crime and travel-care shield laws actively reduce risk despite national border/federal restrictions; no state facility ban or documented targeting found.

Complaint-enforced school/government facility ban and flag hostility are traveler-facing universal exposure; partial hate-crime/ID protections insufficient to restore above restrictive national baseline.
Protective law and public-accommodation recourse help visitors, but recent murders, national border risk and unresolved sanctuary reach keep this below safer shield states.
